newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-WOUDA AND WARNECKE BETTER OWN WORLD RECORDS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-WOUDA AND WARNECKE BETTER OWN WORLD RECORDS.

text.p: In-form Dutchman Marcel Wouda bettered his own 400 metres individual medley shortcourse world record set just a week ago with a time of four minutes 05.41 seconds at a World Cup meeting on Saturday.

The 24-year-old Wouda, who set the previous mark of 4:05.59 last Saturday in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, just missed out on a medal at last year's Olympics but picked up three titles at the European sprint championships in December.

German Mark Warnecke also lowered his own 50 metres breaststroke shortcourse world record with a time of 26.97 seconds. Warnecke, the reigning 100 metres breaststroke shortcourse world champion, set the previous record of 27.00 two years ago in Gelsenkirchen, Germany.
On a fine day for Gemany, Warnecke's compatriot Joerg Hofmman broke the 400 freestyle shortcourse European record with 3:40.58, bettering his own mark of 3:40.78 set last Saturday in Gelsenkirchen.
